_doc: THE ADVERSARIAL REVIEW LEDGER (R ruled 2026-08-07: make review structural, not episodic). Append-only. REQUIRED ROW SHAPE — every field is read by gate A10 and a missing one blocks the streak rather than being ignored: { at: 'YYYY-MM-DD' (chronological; rows must be non-decreasing, or a reorder could manufacture a streak), reviewer: a name on INDEPENDENT_REVIEWERS in go-live-interlock.test.ts (the authoring lane can never satisfy the bar; a 'self:' row RESETS it but never satisfies it), findings: THE NUMBER (not '3 (all fixed)', not 'three', not absent — a count that is not a number cannot be zero), moneyDigest: the money-core digest AS REVIEWED — run the interlock suite and copy the printed value; a clean row vouches for THAT tree and expires the moment any money-core file changes, scope: free text for humans, plus notes. ⚠ ROWS ARE PASSES OVER *THIS LANE'S* MONEY-PATH COMMITS. A pass this worker RUNS OVER ANOTHER LANE never belongs here: its row would count toward THIS lane's go-live bar — advancing our own bar by reviewing someone else's code, the correlated-observer trap wearing a different hat. ⚠⚠ THE FIRST CUT OF THIS MECHANISM WAS MEASURED TO PERMIT A FLIP FIVE WAYS (SpectrumContracts, 2026-08-07): an annotated findings count, an absent findings key, a self row with findings being DELETED rather than resetting, the authoring lane naming itself unprefixed, and one reviewer supplying both lenses via a trailing space. Every one is now a test. The rows below predate the moneyDigest requirement and therefore CANNOT satisfy the bar — which is correct: they reviewed a tree that has since moved.

rows.scope: 0a82983 - the four never-independently-reviewed modules (batcher, plan-legs, displayed-vs-signed, submission-store) and the three e036ac6 fixes
rows.notes: Four-lens independent pass over the four never-reviewed modules, attacking the three e036ac6 FIXES rather than re-finding the bugs. 26 findings: 2 CRITICAL, 1 CRITICAL-when-live, 6 HIGH. CRITICAL: renewClaim is the ONE writer with no assertWritable, so the 15s heartbeat poisons its own live claim and no in-product path recovers it (adding the guard leaves all 119 tests passing); and markClaimAmbiguous sits INSIDE recordSubmission's catch, so a clock that leaves the window after the wallet answered skips the whole recovery and the next run re-submits and reports done - the double-buy the module exists to prevent, with no attacker. I verified both structurally myself before relaying. CRITICAL-when-live: the shown and composed `optional` are the SAME property of the SAME object (assemble-batch.ts:301 and :363 both from planned.legs), so the strict gate cannot see a shared wrong value - measured, a planted plan-legs defect made two healthy legs skippable and the gate returned null while 132 of the author's tests passed. HIGH: the Infinity sentinel makes worst.ratio sort by INSERTION ORDER (Infinity-Infinity=NaN), so a 1% leg is named worst while an 80% unconsented leg hides at index 10 - the original harm re-created one layer up; Infinity serialises to null and reads back as 0, inverting a policy fail-open; and a submission-store test asserts `find(...)?.ambiguous` toBeUndefined, which is satisfied by DELETING the row - a planted delete survived all 1963 tests. Answering the author's own questions: Infinity is NOT the right sentinel; the two counters DO separate the two directions but rest on inconsistent definitions and different units; and the false-refusal side of reject-don't-clamp is worse than the theft it prevents. Also measured: worst.ratio on the module's own canonical case is 11.999999999999996, so a policy written as >= 12 does not fire on it. A REAL pass - the streak stays at zero.
